submission.description: Brick and block cavity wall carried up as a parapet round a flat roof. Felt turned up the wall a little, stone coping on top.

inspiration.title: Warm roof at a parapet
principles: Insulation sits above the deck; the membrane sits above the insulation.
The membrane turns up the parapet as an upstand.
Wall insulation and roof insulation meet so the warm line is unbroken.

inspiration.title: Keeping water out of the top of the wall
principles: A coping sheds water away from the wall face and has a drip.
A damp-proof layer under the coping stops water soaking down the wall.

points.title: Upstand height
points.reason: The felt only turns up the wall a little. Water blown against the parapet can get over it.
points.why: The membrane has to turn up high enough that standing or wind-driven water cannot get over the top of it and into the wall.
points.question: How far above the finished roof should the membrane turn up, and where would you finish its top edge?

points.title: Nothing under the coping
points.reason: There is no damp-proof layer shown under the coping, so water that gets past the coping joints can run down inside the wall.
points.why: Coping joints are not watertight forever. A layer under the coping catches what gets through.
points.question: What would stop water that gets through a coping joint from soaking down the wall?

points.title: Stone or metal coping
points.reason: Both can work. The choice depends on the look of the building, cost and how the joints are made.
points.why: This is a design judgement rather than a rule.

points.title: Insulation carried up
points.reason: You carried the cavity insulation up into the parapet, which keeps the warm line going round the corner.
points.why: A break in the insulation at the roof edge is a cold spot where condensation can form.
